why.title: Your why
why.intro: The foundation of your journey. On hard days, we'll remind you of the reason that brought you here.

you.title: About you
you.intro: Who you are today: country, age, languages, education, and work.

goal.title: Your goal
goal.intro: Why, for how long, and when you want to go.

household.title: Who is going with you
household.intro: Spouse, children, other dependents, and pets. This is the most important section for special situations.

health.title: Health
health.intro: Each person's conditions, medication, and care, so the right tasks are included and costs can be estimated.

money.title: Money
money.intro: Family income, savings, housing, car, and commitments. This feeds your moving budget.

pref.title: Preferences and lifestyle
pref.intro: Climate, city size, pace of life. What you like matters as much as the requirements.

dest.title: Destination
dest.intro: Where you are thinking of going and what matters most in that choice.

history.title: History with the U.S.
history.intro: Visits, visas, and people you know there.

docs.title: Documents
docs.intro: Yes or no only: no files are uploaded.

career.title: Professional profile
career.intro: The careers of those who will work: you and your spouse. It's the basis for pointing to the visa paths worth learning about.

moment.title: Your moment
moment.intro: How your life is right now, so your journey starts at the right pace. Everything is optional.

rhythm.title: Your pace
rhythm.intro: How often you want to follow your journey and what motivates you.

reason.label: Why do you want to live in the United States?
reason.why: Your reason is the foundation of your journey. It's shown back to you on the home screen and at reflection points.

reasonOther.label: What is the other reason?
reasonOther.why: So we can record your reason in your own words.

reasonText.label: In your own words, why do you want to go?
reasonText.why: Reading your own reason, written by you, helps you keep going on hard days.

expect.label: What do you hope will change in your life?
expect.why: It helps you check, along the way, whether the journey still makes sense for you.

fears.label: What worries you most about this move?
fears.why: Knowing what worries you helps the journey address those topics early.

options.legal: Doing something wrong in the process

fearsOther.label: What is the other worry?
fearsOther.why: So we can record your worry in your own words.

giveUp.label: What are you willing to give up?
giveUp.why: Every move involves trade-offs. Thinking about them early helps you decide with awareness.

nationalities.label: What is your nationality? If you have more than one, select all.
nationalities.why: Nationality affects visa types, agreements between countries, and some available programs.

residence.label: Which country do you live in today?
residence.why: It determines the consulate, local documents, and the tasks for leaving the country.

birthYear.label: What year were you born?
birthYear.why: Age affects visa types, health plans, and some tasks.

sex.label: What is your sex, as shown on your passport?
sex.why: Used only to show the questions and tasks that apply to each person (for example, pregnancy).

languages.label: Which languages do you speak?
languages.why: It helps plan your adaptation and find communities that speak your language.

english.label: How is your English today?
english.why: It shapes your English study plan and whether language tests may be needed.

options.basic: I understand simple words and phrases
options.intermediate: I can get by day to day (grocery store, restaurant)
options.advanced: I can talk about almost anything
options.fluent: I can work and study in English

education.label: What is your highest completed level of education?
education.why: Education affects visa types and diploma recognition.

field.label: What is your field of study?
field.why: It helps find the diploma recognition tasks for your field.

occupation.label: What is your current profession or occupation?
occupation.why: Your profession affects visa paths and the job market.

experienceYears.label: How many years have you worked in this field?
experienceYears.why: Experience counts for some types of work visas.

regulated.label: Does your profession require a license or registration to practice? (e.g., medicine, nursing, law, engineering, accounting)
regulated.why: Regulated professions usually require a license in the destination state.

workStatus.label: What is your work situation today?
workStatus.why: It affects income, visa path, and taxes.

options.remote_foreign: Remote work for a company in another country

purpose.label: What is the main reason for your move?
purpose.why: Your reason defines the possible paths and the first tasks of your journey.

options.transfer: Be transferred by the company I work for
options.marriage: Marry or live with a U.S. citizen

duration.label: How long do you want to stay?
duration.why: The length of your stay greatly changes the phases and tasks of your journey.

departure.label: When would you like to go?
departure.why: This is the base of your timeline: the journey is planned backward from this date.

has.label: What do you already have today?
has.why: It shows where your journey starts.

options.school_admission: Admission to a school or university
options.us_relative: A relative who lives in the U.S.
options.company_branch: A company with a U.S. branch

sponsorship.label: What type of visa will the employer sponsor?
sponsorship.why: Temporary visas and Green Cards follow different paths and timelines. If you don't know, the journey explains the difference.

familyLink.label: Who is your relative in the U.S.?
familyLink.why: The type of relationship and your relative's status change the possible paths.

options.child_citizen: Son or daughter who is a citizen
options.sibling_citizen: Brother or sister who is a citizen

studyLevel.label: What do you want to study?
studyLevel.why: Each type of program has its own path and tasks.

investRange.label: How much are you thinking of investing? (in USD)
investRange.why: The investment amount changes the possible paths for starting a business.

partner.label: Do you have a spouse or partner?
partner.why: Who goes with you changes the tasks, documents, and budget.

options.undecided: Yes, but we don't know yet if they're coming

partnerUnion.label: What type of union do you have?
partnerUnion.why: Not every type of union is treated the same way in visa processes. The journey shows the general rule with an official source.

children.label: How many children are going with you? Count all of them, of any age, including adults.
children.why: Each child may need their own tasks: school, documents, health.
children.hint: Enter 0 if no children are going.

otherChildren.label: Is any of these children from another relationship?
otherChildren.why: The other parent's authorization for travel may be required.

custody.label: Does the other parent agree with the move?
custody.why: It determines whether the journey includes travel authorization tasks.

options.sole: I have sole custody or the other parent has passed away

dependents.label: Besides your spouse and children, is anyone who depends on you coming along? (e.g., father, mother, grandmother, sibling)
dependents.why: Other dependents usually need their own path and care planning.
dependents.hint: Enter 0 if no one else is coming.

pets.label: Will you bring pets?
pets.why: Animals have transport and entry rules.

leftBehind.label: Will anyone who depends on you stay in your country?
leftBehind.why: It adds planning tasks for those who stay: care, powers of attorney, sending money.

leftBehindList.label: Who will stay in your country?
leftBehindList.why: It helps plan support for those who stay.

sex.label: What is your spouse's sex, as shown on their passport?
sex.why: Used only to show the questions and tasks that apply to each person (for example, pregnancy).

birthYear.label: What year was your spouse born?
birthYear.why: Age affects health plans and some tasks.

workStatus.label: What is your spouse's work situation today?
workStatus.why: It shows which career questions make sense and helps plan the family's income in the U.S.

english.label: How is your spouse's English?
english.why: It helps plan the family's English and who can work in the U.S.

occupation.label: What is your spouse's profession or occupation?
occupation.why: It helps think about the family's income in the U.S.

nickname.label: What would you like to call this child in the app?
nickname.why: Just to identify them in the journey. Use a nickname or leave it blank.

birth.label: Month and year of birth
birth.why: The journey takes years. With the date, the app calculates the age at each point of the timeline, because some rules depend on it.

sex.label: What is their sex, as shown on their documents?
sex.why: Used only to show the questions and tasks that apply to each person (for example, pregnancy).

school.label: What stage of school are they in?
school.why: It defines school and school-record tasks.

specialNeeds.label: Do they have a disability or need ongoing care?
specialNeeds.why: It adds care, services, and cost tasks to the journey. Details go in the Health section.

english.label: Do they speak English?
english.why: It helps plan their adaptation at school and in daily life.

nickname.label: What would you like to call this person in the app?
nickname.why: Just to identify them in the journey. Use a nickname or leave it blank.

relation.label: How are they related to you?
relation.why: The relationship changes the possible paths for this person.

birth.label: Month and year of birth
birth.why: With the date, the app calculates the age at each point of the timeline.

sex.label: What is their sex, as shown on their documents?
sex.why: Used only to show the questions and tasks that apply to each person (for example, pregnancy).

dependency.label: What kind of dependence?
dependency.why: It helps plan care and budget.

options.care: Needs care but has their own income

conditions.label: Do any of these apply?
conditions.why: To include health tasks in the journey and estimate costs in the U.S. It stays only on this device.

options.chronic: Chronic illness (e.g., diabetes, heart disease, kidney disease)
options.mental: Mental health (e.g., depression, anxiety, bipolar disorder)

autismLevel.label: Autism support level
autismLevel.why: It helps size the services and care to research at the destination.

intellectualDegree.label: Degree of intellectual disability
intellectualDegree.why: It helps size the services and care to research at the destination.

autonomy.label: In daily life, this person…
autonomy.why: It defines important tasks, such as legal representation of an adult in the U.S. and care planning.

options.help: Needs help with daily activities (bathing, eating, dressing)

caregiver.label: Who is the main caregiver?
caregiver.why: Caregiving takes someone's time, and that goes into the budget and work planning.

medications.label: Do they take ongoing medication?
medications.why: Ongoing medication creates tasks: initial supply, prescriptions, entry rules, and a doctor in the U.S.
medications.hint: Add each medication. If none, you can skip.

therapies.label: Do they have any regular treatment or therapy?
therapies.why: It helps research availability and cost at the destination.

equipmentList.label: Do they use any of this equipment?
equipmentList.why: Equipment may have transport rules and costs at the destination.

equipmentOther.label: What other equipment?
equipmentOther.why: Just to include it in the journey.

specialistsList.label: Are they followed by any of these specialists?
specialistsList.why: It helps plan continued care in the U.S.

specialistsOther.label: What other specialist?
specialistsOther.why: Just to include it in the journey.

pregnancy.label: Current pregnancy or planned within the next 2 years?
pregnancy.why: It affects the health plan, costs, and timeline.

vaccines.label: Are vaccinations up to date?
vaccines.why: Some visa processes require vaccinations and a medical exam.

earnersNow.label: Who earns income in your family today?
earnersNow.why: A family with a single source of income is more exposed if it stops. The journey takes this into account.

options.passive: Income that doesn't depend on work (rent, pension)

earnersUS.label: Who plans to work in the U.S.?
earnersUS.why: Each person's work authorization depends on the visa type. The journey shows the general rule with an official source.

partnerAvailability.label: Would your spouse be available to work?
partnerAvailability.why: It helps calculate the family's possible income and the time spent on caregiving.

options.no: No, {partnerSex, select, male {he's} female {she's} other {they're}} a full-time caregiver

otherSources.label: Do you have, or could you have, other sources of income?
otherSources.why: The journey shows only legal options for additional income.

options.remote_home: Remote work for a company or clients in my country
options.rent_home: Renting out property in my country
options.none: I don't see other options right now

saved.label: How much have you already saved for the move?
saved.why: With this amount, the app calculates how much is left to reach the goal.

monthlySaving.label: How much can you save per month?
monthlySaving.why: With this amount, the app calculates how long it will take to reach the goal.

bring.label: How much do you plan to bring? (in USD)
bring.why: The app compares it with the goal suggested by the moving budget.

expectedIncomeUS.label: What is the annual salary offered? (in USD, before taxes)
expectedIncomeUS.why: It's the base for calculating whether income covers expenses in the U.S.

employerBenefits.label: What does the employer offer besides salary?
employerBenefits.why: Benefits change the budget a lot, especially health insurance.

income.label: Will you keep any income after the move?
income.why: Ongoing income helps the budget, but you need to confirm whether your visa type allows it and which taxes apply.

incomeMonthly.label: About how much per month? (in USD)
incomeMonthly.why: It goes into the income vs. expenses calculation.

housingPlan.label: How do you plan to live in the U.S. at first?
housingPlan.why: Renting or buying greatly changes upfront and monthly costs.

carPlan.label: What about a car?
carPlan.why: A car has purchase, insurance, registration, and state fee costs.

carCount.label: How many cars?
carCount.why: Each car goes into the budget.

scoutingTrips.label: Do you plan to visit the U.S. before the move to see the destination?
scoutingTrips.why: Trips before the move go into the pre-move costs.

scoutingPeople.label: Who will go on these trips?
scoutingPeople.why: It helps estimate flights and lodging.

moveBelongings.label: What do you plan to bring in the move?
moveBelongings.why: It helps estimate the cost of the move.

assets.label: What will you do with your assets (home, car)?
assets.why: Selling, renting, or keeping creates tasks and changes the budget.

debts.label: Do you have active debts or loans?
debts.why: Ongoing commitments go into the monthly budget.

debtsContinue.label: Will they keep being paid after the move?
debtsContinue.why: If so, the payment goes into monthly expenses.

debtsMonthly.label: About how much per month?
debtsMonthly.why: It goes into monthly expenses as a commitment in your home country.

runway.label: For how many months does the money need to last until you have income in the U.S.?
runway.why: It helps size the emergency fund.

climate.label: What climate do you prefer?
climate.why: Climate weighs heavily on well-being. The destination comparison takes it into account.

heat.label: How do you handle strong, humid heat?
heat.why: Someone who can't stand heat shouldn't get a place with long, humid summers as the main suggestion.

snow.label: And snow and intense cold?
snow.why: It helps point out conflicts between the destination and what you like.

placeSize.label: Where do you picture yourself living?
placeSize.why: City size changes cost of living, transportation, and routine.

leisure.label: What do you like to have nearby?
leisure.why: It helps compare destinations with your lifestyle.

car.label: Do you plan to live without a car?
car.why: In many places in the U.S., a car is almost essential. This changes the choice of destination.

pace.label: What pace of life suits you?
pace.why: It helps compare destinations with your lifestyle.

community.label: Do you want to live near people from your country or who speak your language?
community.why: A community nearby can make adapting easier.

options.some: It would be nice, but not essential

hobbies.label: What do you like to do in your free time?
hobbies.why: Hobbies help choose the place and are the most natural way to make friends and build a routine in a new country.

feelGood.label: What makes you feel good when you're tired or down?
feelGood.why: On hard days of the journey, the app reminds you of what does you good and suggests it as a reward.

outings.label: What outings do you enjoy most?
outings.why: It helps compare cities and think about family leisure in the budget.

domesticTravel.label: Do you like traveling within your country to discover new places?
domesticTravel.why: Getting to know the new country is part of adapting, and trips go into the budget.

options.not_interested: It's not something I look for

familyPriorities.label: What is a priority for your family?
familyPriorities.why: Family priorities weigh in the destination comparison.

known.label: Do you already know where you want to go?
known.why: If you don't know yet, the journey helps compare states with your preferences.

places.label: Which states?
places.why: The state determines taxes, cost of living, climate, and services.

cityList.label: Any city in mind?
cityList.why: It makes comparisons of cost, climate and taxes more precise.

why.label: Why this place?
why.why: It helps compare the destination with what matters to you.

criteria.label: What matters most in the choice? (choose up to 3)
criteria.why: It defines what the destination comparison will highlight.

options.community: Community from my country or language

visited.label: Have you been to the U.S.?
visited.why: It helps plan visits and your adaptation.

visa.label: Do you have, or have you ever had, a U.S. visa?
visa.why: It helps set up the first document tasks.

network.label: Do you know anyone who lives in the U.S.?
network.why: A support network makes a difference when you arrive.

complication.label: Is there anything in your history, or that of anyone in the family who's going, that could cause complications? (e.g., a denied visa, staying longer than allowed, a criminal record)
complication.why: We don't ask for details. If the answer is yes, the journey recommends seeing an immigration lawyer right at the start.

passport.label: Passport
passport.why: An expired or soon-to-expire passport becomes a high-priority task and goes into the costs.

certificates.label: Which of these documents do you already have on hand?
certificates.why: Missing documents become tasks. No files are uploaded.

driverLicense.label: Do you have a driver's license?
driverLicense.why: It helps plan getting a driver's license in the destination state.

life.label: How is your life right now?
life.why: Nobody needs to be perfect to start. Your answer only adjusts the pace: in a hard phase, the journey starts lighter.

events.label: Has anything major happened in your life in the last 12 months?
events.why: Big changes take energy. Knowing this helps the journey respect where you are.

options.own_health: A health problem of my own

decision.label: Where are you in your decision to live in the U.S.?
decision.why: If you're still getting to know the idea, the journey starts by exploring before deciding. Concluding it's not for you is a good outcome too.

options.exploring: I'm still getting to know the idea
options.decided: I've decided I want to go

partnerSupport.label: How does your spouse feel about the move?
partnerSupport.why: A move like this works better when the couple is on the same page. If you're not there yet, the journey brings those conversations early.

options.aligned: They want it as much as I do

familySupport.label: Do the people close to you support the idea?
familySupport.why: Support makes a difference on hard days. Your answer helps the journey remind you where to find strength.

nationalities.label: What is your spouse's nationality? If more than one, select all.
nationalities.why: Each adult's nationality can open or close different visa paths. Sometimes the best path is through the spouse.

education.label: What is your spouse's highest completed education?
education.why: Each adult's education helps point to the visa paths worth learning about.

field.label: What is your spouse's field of study?
field.why: It helps connect education with profession and the U.S. job market.

experienceYears.label: How many years has your spouse worked in {sex, select, male {his} female {her} other {their}} field?
experienceYears.why: Years of experience help point to visa paths and plan the job search.

regulated.label: Does your spouse's profession require a registration or license to practice?
regulated.why: Licensed professions usually require validating the degree and license in the destination state.

sector.label: What area is the work in?
sector.why: The area helps point to visa paths and to each state's job market.

role.label: What is the current job title or role?
role.why: The title shows the kind of work done today and helps compare with U.S. job openings.

level.label: What career level is it today?
level.why: Level, leadership and responsibilities matter for some work-based visa paths.

multinational.label: Does the company have a branch, headquarters or related company in the U.S.?
multinational.why: Some companies transfer employees to the U.S. Knowing this helps point to that path.

companyTime.label: How long have you worked at this company?
companyTime.why: Time at the company helps see whether the transfer path is worth studying.

achievements.label: Which of these achievements are part of the career? Select only what can be proven.
achievements.why: Some visa paths based on professional merit ask for evidence of achievements like these. Selecting guarantees nothing: it only shows what is worth learning about, always with the official source.

options.awards: Awards or recognition in the field
options.associations: Membership in associations that only accept outstanding professionals
options.media: Press or trade publication articles about the work
options.judge: Judging others' work (panel, jury, peer review)
options.contributions: Recognized original contributions to the field (e.g., patents, methods, products)
options.exhibitions: Work displayed at exhibitions, showcases or festivals
options.leading_role: Leading role in a distinguished organization
options.high_salary: High salary compared to the field

usJobSearch.label: Have you looked for work in the U.S.?
usJobSearch.why: Shows where the job search stands and which tasks come first.

sameField.label: Do you want to stay in the same field in the U.S.?
sameField.why: Changing fields changes the possible paths and the preparation tasks (courses, certifications).

principal.label: Who in the family has the strongest professional profile to lead the visa application?
principal.why: Sometimes the best path is through the spouse, and the family goes along. The journey can show both paths.

cadence.label: How often do you want to follow your journey?
cadence.why: The pace is yours. The journey adapts to it, with no pressure.

weeklyTime.label: How much time per week can you dedicate?
weeklyTime.why: It sets the size of the tasks suggested each week.

rewards.label: What small rewards motivate you?
rewards.why: Celebrating small wins helps you keep going. You choose your rewards.

options.free_time: Some free time just for me

rewardsOther.label: What is your reward?
rewardsOther.why: So we can suggest your reward when you complete tasks.
